en.title: Collecting Data Within Two Steps on a Tree
en.description:
You may start from any tree node; visiting a node collects all data within at most 2 edges of it. Find the minimum number of edge traversals needed to collect all data and return to the starting node. The source example with n=11 has only 9 edges and an isolated node 5, so it is not a valid tree; this site replaces it with a valid example.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains n data flags, each 0/1, followed by n−1 lines of edges u v. 2≤n≤100000, 0≤u,v<n, and the input is guaranteed to be a valid undirected tree.
en.output: Output the minimum number of edge traversals; output 0 when there is no data or no movement is needed.
en.explanation: For a chain of length 6 with data at both ends, traversing the core edge twice suffices, so the answer is 2; a star tree and a tree with no data both give 0.
hints: First repeatedly delete leaves that have no data, then delete the two outermost layers of leaves of the remaining tree at once. Each remaining edge is traversed twice.
